study.title: Moses: rescue, flight and a remembered covenant

summary.text: Moses survives the decree against Hebrew boys through the actions of his family and Pharaoh’s daughter. His attempt to intervene in violence leads to flight to Midian. The closing scene shifts from his new household to Israel’s cries and God’s attention to the covenant.

participants.text: Moses’ mother and sister, Pharaoh’s daughter and her attendants protect the child. Later, Moses meets Reuel’s daughters, marries Zipporah and names his son Gershom. The enslaved Israelites remain central even when the narrative follows Moses elsewhere.

setting.text: The story moves from the Nile in Egypt to a well and household in Midian. The king of Egypt is not named here; the chapter alone does not establish a date or identify a particular pharaoh.

literaryContext.text: Read this chapter between the oppression of Exodus 1 and the calling of Exodus 3. Deliverance is not yet accomplished: the ending introduces the covenant as the frame for the action that follows, rather than making Moses’ escape the conclusion.

outline.title: Violence, flight and a new household

connections.explanation: The promise to Abram already includes oppression and a later departure; compare that promise with the covenant recalled here.
God’s hearing and seeing become a commission to Moses in the next chapter.
